skill.name: pixijs-filters
skill.description: Use this skill when applying visual effects to PixiJS v8 containers via the filter pipeline. Covers built-in filters (AlphaFilter, BlurFilter, ColorMatrixFilter, DisplacementFilter, NoiseFilter), custom Filter.from() with GLSL/WGSL, options (resolution, padding, antialias, blendRequired), filterArea optimization, pixi-filters community package. Triggers on: filters, BlurFilter, ColorMatrixFilter, DisplacementFilter, NoiseFilter, Filter.from, GLSL filter, pixi-filters, filterArea.
skill.summary: Apply and optimize PixiJS v8 filters with guidance on built-in effects, custom shaders, community filters, and renderer compatibility.

content.user_title: Apply and Optimize PixiJS v8 Filters
content.value_statement: PixiJS filter effects can fail when shader APIs, renderer settings, or package imports do not match version 8. This skill guides filter setup, custom shaders, and performance tuning with focused examples.
actual_capabilities: Guide setup and chaining of alpha, blur, color matrix, displacement, and noise filters.
Explain custom GLSL filters with Filter.from(), typed uniform resources, and animation ticker updates.
Show current pixi-filters imports for adjustment and glow effects.
Explain resolution, padding, antialiasing, filterArea, and shared filter instances.
Identify obsolete constructors, legacy package imports, and inefficient per-child filter applications.
Explain advanced blend mode imports, high-DPI resolution settings, and WebGL back buffer requirements.
limitations: Targets PixiJS v8 rather than providing complete guidance for earlier versions.
Provides reference instructions and snippets, not a standalone application or automated test suite.
Mentions WGSL and WebGPU program selection but does not include a complete WGSL filter example.
Rendering quality and performance require verification with your assets, renderer, and target devices.

use_cases.title: Add game scene effects
use_cases.description: Apply blur, color adjustments, displacement, or noise to game sprites and containers with appropriate filter ordering.

use_cases.title: Update filter integrations
use_cases.description: Replace obsolete filter constructors and community package imports when migrating a rendering interface to PixiJS v8.

use_cases.title: Tune custom visual effects
use_cases.description: Structure shader uniforms and reduce filter overhead through container grouping, resolution settings, and explicit filter areas.

prompt_templates.prompt: Show how to apply a BlurFilter to my PixiJS v8 sprite. Use strength 4 and explain the quality setting.

prompt_templates.title: Combine scene effects
prompt_templates.prompt: Combine blur and brightness adjustments on a PixiJS v8 container. Explain filter order and set filterArea for an 800 by 600 scene.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: chain filters and define known bounds.

prompt_templates.title: Migrate legacy filters
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my filter code for PixiJS v8 compatibility. Replace obsolete constructors and @pixi/filter-* imports, and check WebGL back buffer requirements.
prompt_templates.scenario: Experienced: update an existing filter integration.

prompt_templates.title: Build an animated custom filter
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a PixiJS v8 GLSL wave filter with Filter.from(), typed uTime resources, and ticker updates. Explain WebGPU coverage and performance tradeoffs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: design a custom shader and evaluate renderer constraints.

output_examples.input: My scene slows down after I add blur to every child.
output: Apply one BlurFilter to the parent container when the intended visual result permits it.
Set filterArea when the affected region has known dimensions.
Compare lower filter resolution and blur quality on target devices.

output_examples.input: My advanced blend mode looks partially applied on a high-DPI render target.
output: Import the advanced blend modes module before assigning the blend mode.
Enable useBackBuffer when initializing the WebGL renderer.
Set the default filter resolution to inherit before creating affected objects, then check memory use and visual output.

output_examples.input: My custom filter uses the old vertex, fragment, uniforms constructor.
output: Replace positional constructor arguments with the PixiJS v8 options object.
Wrap shader sources with GlProgram.from() or GpuProgram.from() for the required renderer.
Group explicitly typed uniforms in resources and keep textures as separate resources.

best_practices: Apply shared effects to a parent container when the visual result permits it, and set filterArea for known bounds.
Use v8 options objects, typed uniform resources, and current community filter import paths.
Test filter resolution and back buffer settings on each supported renderer and target device.
anti_patterns: Using positional Filter constructor arguments or legacy @pixi/filter-* packages in a v8 project.
Creating identical filters on every child when one parent filter provides the intended result.
Enabling blendRequired filters on WebGL without initializing useBackBuffer.

faq.question: Which PixiJS version does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets PixiJS v8 filter APIs and highlights incompatible constructor and package patterns from earlier versions.

faq.question: Which built-in effects are covered?
faq.answer: It covers AlphaFilter, BlurFilter, ColorMatrixFilter, DisplacementFilter, and NoiseFilter, including configuration and chaining examples.

faq.question: Does it include custom shader guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It demonstrates a GLSL fragment filter with typed resources and ticker updates, plus direct graphics program construction.

faq.question: Are the custom examples ready for both WebGL and WebGPU?
faq.answer: No. The complete custom shader example uses GLSL. WebGPU requires a corresponding GPU program, and no complete WGSL example is included.

faq.question: How can I reduce filter overhead?
faq.answer: Use parent container effects where suitable, define filterArea for known bounds, and evaluate lower resolution or blur quality.

faq.question: Does the skill install packages or verify rendering automatically?
faq.answer: No. It contains Markdown guidance and code examples. Package setup and rendering checks remain part of your project workflow.
